headline: Day Use and Backcountry Permit Protocols
reservation: Daily vehicle permits are mandatory for park entry and should be obtained via the Ontario Parks reservation system up to five days in advance. Backcountry camping requires a separate specific permit for designated zones. Visitors must distinguish between vehicle entry and overnight stays, as the latter can book out during peak summer weekends.

days.title: Superior Shoreline and Canyons

stops.name: Thunder Bay Lookout
stops.detail: Drive to this cantilevered platform for a dramatic view over Lake Superior without a strenuous hike.

stops.name: Sea Lion
stops.detail: Hike a short section of the Kabeyun Trail to see this distinct diabase rock formation arching over the water.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for park interior roads; gravel sections require slower speeds.
days.note: The road to the Thunder Bay Lookout is steep and may not be suitable for all vehicle types.

days.title: The Giant's Summit
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from Marie Louise Lake

stops.name: Top of the Giant Trail
stops.detail: Commit to this demanding ascent for the most famous view in the park, overlooking the Sibley Peninsula.

stops.name: Tee Harbour
stops.detail: Relax at this sheltered bay along the Kabeyun Trail, a popular spot for cyclists and hikers alike.

days.driving: Walking/Hiking; allow 6 to 8 hours for the full Top of the Giant round trip.
days.note: Start early to avoid mid-day heat on the exposed rock faces and carry sufficient water.

days.title: Silver Islet History

stops.name: Silver Islet General Store
stops.detail: Visit this historic landmark to learn about the 19th-century silver mine that once sat beneath the lake.

stops.name: Middlebrun Bay
stops.detail: Hike to a secluded sandy beach and continue to Finlay Bay for a quieter experience on the park's eastern side.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for transit to the southern tip of the peninsula; parking is limited.
days.note: Silver Islet is a private community located at the end of the park road; stay on designated public paths.

intel.title: Trailhead Saturation
intel.text: The South Kabeyun trailhead often reaches capacity by mid-morning. Utilize the secondary lots at Marie Louise Lake if primary areas are full, though this adds walking distance.

intel.title: Shield Topography Interference
intel.text: Expect near-total signal loss at the base of the cliffs and along remote shoreline sections. Emergency communication devices are recommended for backcountry hikers.

intel.title: Gateway Supplies
intel.text: There is no fuel available within the park boundaries. The nearest reliable service stations are located along Highway 11/17 or in Thunder Bay.

intel.title: Black Fly Season
intel.text: Early summer visits may coincide with peak biting insect activity. Trail conditions can be muddy through June; late August offers the most stable hiking weather.

intel.title: Remote Trail Safety
intel.text: The Top of the Giant trail involves a significant elevation gain and rugged terrain. Ensure you are off the summit well before dusk, as the descent is difficult in low light.

plan.arrival: Pick up supplies in Thunder Bay before driving the 80km to the Sibley Peninsula; check in at the Marie Louise Lake gatehouse for permits.
plan.vehicle: Most park roads are accessible by car, but high-clearance vehicles are recommended for the Thunder Bay Lookout road.
plan.goldenHour: The Thunder Bay Lookout offers westward views perfect for sunset, provided the park gates remain open during your visit window.
